deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from this page and its neighbours). X is a topological projective plane and Σ=(Δ_i)_{i∈I} is a simple ('stable') arrangement of pseudolines, meaning no three are concurrent. C_st(I) is the set of isomorphism classes of such arrangements labelled by I. Choose a line Δ=Δ_{i0} as the line at infinity and put I_0=I∖{i0}. This gives C_st(I) ≅ C_aff st(I_0), the classes of labelled affine (Euclidean) simple arrangements.

Cutting X along Δ ('Déc(X,Δ)') gives a disk D. Its boundary ∂D is the 2-sheeted cover of Δ. The other pseudolines become a stable system of chords in D indexed by I_0. Their 2n endpoints (n=|I_0|) form a 2n-gon Ĩ_0(ξ) with a free antipodal involution. Its quotient I_0(ξ) is I_0 equipped with the polygonal (dihedral cyclic-order) structure: the order in which the lines meet the line at infinity.

Now fix once and for all a polygonal set S of order 2n with antipodism a_S, and put I_0=S/a_S. On I_0 this induces a quotient polygon structure π_0.
- C̃_st(S) is the set of stable chord systems whose endpoint set is identified with S ('S-épinglées'), modulo S-isomorphism.
- Equivalently, C̃_st(S) consists of wiring diagrams / primitive sorting networks up to commutation, i.e. rhombic tilings of the 2n-gon.

This page states three things.
1. The natural map C̃_st(S) → C_aff st(I_0) has image C^!_aff st(I_0) = C_aff st(I_0,π_0). This is the set of labelled affine stable arrangements whose cyclic order at infinity is exactly π_0.
2. The fibre over ξ is identified with the set of polygonal isomorphisms S ≅ Ĩ_0(ξ) lying over the identity of I_0. These are the isomorphisms making the triangle with the two canonical projections to I_0 commute.
3. This set has cardinality 2, the two elements differing by antipodism. It is a torsor under the deck group Z/2, since a connected antipodal double cover of an n-cycle is unique up to isomorphism.

Consequently |C̃_st(S)| = 2·|C^!_aff st(I_0)|. Check for n=3: there are 2 pinned arrangements (the 2 rhombic tilings of the hexagon) and 1 labelled affine arrangement with fixed order at infinity.

A struck-out example records that for |I_0|=5, C_aff st(I_0) ≅ C_st(I_0⊔{e0}) splits into 6 conjugacy classes under 𝔖_{I_0}. This matches the classical count of 6 simple Euclidean arrangements of 5 (pseudo)lines.

The next page completes the counting. Dividing by the dihedral group D_{I_0} gives the unlabelled affine classes C_aff(n), and orbit–stabilizer relates labelled and unlabelled counts. The factor is n!/2n = (n−1)!/2, the number of polygon structures on I_0. Stabilisers are identified with Aut(X,Σ,Δ). The purpose of the whole computation is to enumerate pseudoline arrangements, projective versus affine, labelled versus unlabelled.
errors: Small gap: the fibre is really the set of pinnings S ≅ Ĩ_0(ξ) modulo automorphisms of the labelled chord system. Identifying it with the set of isomorphisms (cardinality 2) needs that no automorphism of a stable labelled chord system induces the antipodism on endpoints. This holds for n≥3: such a map would reverse every chord and fix every crossing, and a reversed chord has only one fixed cell. It fails for n=2, where the X-shaped crossing is centrally symmetric and the fibre has 1 element. This is consistent with Grothendieck's earlier caveat card I_0 ≥ 3, but the point is not argued on the page.
'Polygonal structure' must be read as unoriented (dihedral) for the next page's count (n−1)!/2 and the group D_{I_0} of order 2n to be consistent. This is implicit, not stated.

ideas.what: Cutting the projective plane along one pseudoline turns a projective arrangement into a disk with a stable chord system, with an antipodal 2n-gon of endpoints double covering the n-gon of directions at infinity.
ideas.modern_name: Affine/Euclidean arrangements from projective ones; wiring diagrams; local sequences / allowable sequences

ideas.what: Pinned ('S-épinglées') stable chord systems in a disk with fixed endpoints, mapping 2:1 onto labelled affine arrangements with prescribed cyclic order at infinity.
ideas.modern_name: Commutation classes of reduced words of w_0 / primitive sorting networks / rhombic tilings of the 2n-gon (OEIS A006245) vs. labelled Euclidean simple arrangements
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goodman–Pollack; Knuth 'Axioms and Hulls' (1992); Elnitsky (1997); Manin–Schechtman higher Bruhat orders (1989)

ideas.what: Fibre of the forgetful map identified as a Z/2-torsor of polygonal isomorphisms over the base (antipodism).
ideas.modern_name: Torsor/fibre counting under deck group of the antipodal double cover

ideas.what: Count of 6 classes of simple affine arrangements of 5 pseudolines (struck out).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, correct but routine piece of enumerative bookkeeping for pseudoline arrangements: pinned chord systems versus labelled affine arrangements versus unlabelled ones. The same relations appear in Goodman–Pollack, Knuth and the sorting-network/rhombic-tiling literature. The torsor-style formulation is typical Grothendieck but adds nothing new. Mild historical interest: in the early 1980s he independently works with the 'pinned disk' model that underlies wiring diagrams and commutation classes.
transcription_corrections: 'C_off st' throughout should read 'C_aff st' (affine stable), consistent with the previous and next pages.
In the struck-out example, 'C_off st(I_0)' should read 'C_aff st(I_0)'. The group is 𝔖_{I_0} (symmetric group), not a fraktur G.
The first line reads 'dont l'image est le sous-ens[emble]' with an underbrace over C_aff st(I_0); the struck symbol before C_aff st(I_0,π_0) is an illegible crossed-out abbreviation.
